newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica profits boosted by expense controls.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica profits boosted by expense controls.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp., the nation's third largest bank, reported strong first quarter earnings, helped by revenue growth and expense controls.
Fleet Financial Group Inc. and Republic Bancorp Inc., reported higher earnings, while Great Western Financial Corp. said its net earnings were hurt by merger related costs.
BankAmerica, California's No. 1 bank reported earnings of $780 million, or $2.05 a share, for the first quarter, compared with $720 million, or $1.79 a share, a year ago.
"It was a solid quarter. The expense controls, revenue growth and loan growth were all encouraging," said Thomas Theurkauf, analyst with Keefe Bruyette Woods.
"We continue to focus on the fundamentals, including effective operating leverage, prudent risk management, and disciplined capital management," said BankAmerica Chairman David Coulter.
The earnings topped Wall Street expectations, but BankAmerica's stock fell $2.25 to $103.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Brown Brothers Harriman analyst Raphael Soifer said while the earnings were good, they were helped in part by the sale of $3 billion of residential first mortgages.
"BankAmerica was better than expected but the main reason was due to a gain on the sale of a mortgage portfolio," Soifer said.
On a conference call, BankAmerica Chief Financial Officer Mike O'Neill said there was good interest in its consumer financial unit, Security Pacific Financial Services, which is up for sale.
Last month, BankAmerica said it planned to sell the unit, with loan assets of $1.4 billion, excluding its executive and professional business unit, which will not be sold.
"A lot of people are calling and we are mid-stream in that process," O'Neill said. BankAmerica has said it hopes to conclude the deal by the second half of 1997.
He cited improvements in many sectors, but said increases in net credit losses and delinquencies were troubling.
"We saw both our net credit losses and delinquenices on cards go up," he said.
"Our increase is less than the industry's but still somewhat troubling," O'Neill said. "Cards as a percentage of our total portfolio is quite small -- about $10 billion.
Separately, Chatsworth, Calif.-based Great Western Financial Corp. said its net earnings for the first quarter were reduced by merger-related costs totalling $33.7 million.
Great Western has agreed to merge with Washington Mutual Inc. and has rejected a takeover bid by rival California savings and loan H.F. Ahmanson and Co.

Great Western posted first quarter net income of $65.7 million, or 44 cents per share, vs. $71.3 million, or 47 cents per share, a year earlier. Great Western stock closed down 50 cents at $40.125 on the NYSE.
Fleet Financial Group Inc. reported an 18 percent increase in first quarter profits.
"We're seeing strong business opportunities across all our core businesses which are producing outstanding results on the bottom line," Chief Executive Terrence Murray said.
Boston-based Fleet said net income was $311 million, or $1.10 per share, in the latest quarter compared with $264 million, or $0.94 pershare a year earlier.
Fleet stock was down 37.5 cents at $57.25 on the NYSE.

Ann Arbor, Mich.-based Republic Bancorp Inc. said earnings for the bank holding company for the quarter rose to $3.96 million, or 23 cents a share, from $2.63 million, or 14 cents a share, earned in the corresponding period in 1996.
Republic Bancorp stock was $12.875, unchanged, on Nasdaq.
